proposed_description: mentre lays two ongoing actions side by side over the same stretch (both verbs typically imperfetto); (non) appena marks a trigger instant (as soon as). Traps: durante + clause (durante takes only a noun), and appena/mentre swapped across the overlap-vs-instant line.

proposed_attributes.canonical_example: Mentre cucinavo, lui guardava la TV. / Appena arrivo, ti chiamo.
proposed_attributes.common_miss: durante + clause (durante cucinavo); appena for an ongoing overlap.

rationale: The connective.time aggregate's description names mentre and (non) appena but no leaf holds them; finché is negation's and prima/dopo has its own leaf. Needed while authoring conn_time_05 and conn_time_06, which are delivered against this proposed id (runtime warns at authoring, strict-rejects at production load, so ratification gates their manifest entry).

proposed_description: Purpose clauses: affinché / perché + subjunctive when a second subject enters; per + infinitive when the subject stays the same; the verb's mood is what separates purpose-perché from cause-perché.
rationale: Commissioned in Architecture_ConnectiveAuthor_purpose_connectives v1 (Smith: 'generally both', resolved via Rev 27 cross-credit). Aggregate proposed with parent connective (exists) so the leaf below has a registered chain.

proposed_description: Choosing the purpose connective and machinery: affinché (formal) / perché (everyday) + subjunctive for a second subject, per + infinitive for a same subject. Cross-credits tense_choice.indicative_vs_subjunctive where the answer produces the subjunctive (Rev 27).

proposed_attributes.canonical_example: Parlo piano affinché tu capisca. / Studio per superare l'esame.
proposed_attributes.common_miss: perché + indicative meant as purpose; per + infinitive with a second subject; affinché + indicative.

rationale: The commissioned leaf (thread names this id). Parent is the sibling proposal above; Architecture mints both on these markpoints landing (6 grammar + 2 translation delivered against it). Boundary per the thread: connective owns the connective CHOICE; tense_choice owns the mood contrast; items where the answer contains the subjunctive dual-cite at credit 0.5 each.
